(n.d.). Yeats included the story in his Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry
(!888).
 289.8: probably not a specific reference. "Holy Joe" colloquially identifies some-
one excessively and ostentatiously pious.
 290: Cruachan, in County Roscommon, the ancient capital of Connacht.
 292: the Delphic Oracle is the supreme oracle in Greek mythology; Plotinus
(205-26g/7o.) is a Greek philosopher. In the Life of Plotinus, the philosopher
Porphyry has Amelius consult the Oracle to learn the fate of Plotinus' soul
after his death.
 292.3: a son of Zeus and Europa in Greek mythology, Rhadamanthus is a ruler
and judge of Elysium, to which certain favored heroes are translated by the
gods and are exempt from death.
 292+ the immortals.
 292.8: Plato, Greek philosopher (ca. 429-347 B.c.). Minos, another son of Zeus
and Europa, is a judge in Elysium.
 292.9: Pythagoras (ca. 582-ca. 507 B.C.), Greek philosopher.
